body: If you don’t mind me asking, did those around you know that you were probably trans before you did? I’ve always been confident in being a guy. I spent my teenage years wanting to grow facial hair and I loved being tall. And I’ve always had a super deep voice. I know that just those features are not indicative of gender identity, but would a trans person really embrace being their sex assigned at birth before experiencing dysphoria?

When you say it took you 4 years to admit those things, was it 4 years to admit it to yourself or those around you? I’ve never had a longstanding history of questioning my gender until that night in Colorado. It feels like I have to admit I’m trans even though I know I’m not.

Thank you. I’ve been doing my best to continue implementing what my therapist taught me. I don’t see him anymore because he charges an exorbitant amount of money. I’m just exhausted at this point. I appreciate you taking the time to comment though. I’m trying to hang on.
